design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (loyalty_points_and_rewards)

1. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}. Root loyalty_ext_delivery_failure_goodwill takes 4 factors; prerequisite loyalty_ext_returned_merchandise_reversal takes 4.

2. Why a good test. A Gold member asks for "the points I'm due" for a damaged dress whose Damaged in Transit claim is approved. The scored grant is not a lookup: the goodwill rule bases a spoiled-line grant on twice the affected order's NET points, and its prerequisite sentence ("The goodwill grant is fixed only after the points ledger carries a reversal entry for every refunded return made against the order the claim concerns.") forces the agent to notice that the trousers returned from the same order were refunded on 2026-07-21 with no reversal on the ledger. The reversal itself is a four-factor calculation over returns, claims, the Unlimited plan and the 12-month ledger. Difficulty = finding the hidden reversal + two layered calculations; no near-synonym tools exist (one reversal tool, one acceptance tool).

3. Scope snapshot. Occupied before: nothing. Claimed now: policies loyalty_ext_returned_merchandise_reversal, loyalty_ext_delivery_failure_goodwill; tools post_points_reversal_46de2c04 (agent), accept_goodwill_points_7ea0a08d (user). Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisites, factors [4,5,4]): missing-points adjustment, tier upgrade and birthday make-good — an independent chain (spend -> tier -> birthday) touching none of this task's policies or tools.

4. Base-defect route-around (recorded, base untouched). (a) The blueprint names exactly one customer-owned write (closure confirmation), whose only figure is the whole positive balance and admits no load-bearing factor; the skill needs a user write with a 4-6 factor computation in every task and disjoint tools. Route: the goodwill grant is credited on the member's own acceptance (a goodwill offer settles the member's complaint; only she can accept it) — base goodwill names no actor, so nothing is overridden on that point. (b) The DSL has no calendar-year window; "goodwill posted in the current calendar year" is computed with within_months = current month number, exact when frozen_time is the last day of a 31-day month (2026-07-31 here). (c) Loyalty compute is scoped to the membership; the claim and the return are reached through their record status (the claim in status approved, the return in status settled), which is how the rules name them; the world holds exactly one of each.

5. Policies, refs, triggers, overwrite. Goodwill also declares (round 2) that a grant is made while the claim stands approved and a resolved claim is closed to a further grant, superseding the base 'approved or resolved' eligibility sentence. Reversal: base_policy_refs [loyalty_evt_points_reversal]; trigger state_due (refund issued, reversal owed); overwrite declares the two base sentences replaced (fixed original multiplier; full reversal of refunded points). Goodwill: refs [loyalty_evt_bonus_points, loyalty_evt_goodwill_points]; trigger on_request; overwrite replaces "The grant equals the goodwill_points_per_case_cap ..." with the uplifted, capped grant. Inherited unchanged: active-status gate, one grant per claim, documented failure (approved/resolved claim), once per bonus reference, per-case and annual caps (still binding), reversal only while active/suspended and once per return and order.

6. Factor card (world at handling time; baseline figure = result with that factor at its fall-through).
Reversal (expected 22, all-baseline 62):
 - return_record_multiplier (method): ledger 12 months ending 2026-07-31 -> reversed spend 0, earning entries 7 -> share 0% with >= 6 entries -> multiplier 1.00 (baseline original 1.50 -> 33). Near-miss: the 2025-05-21 earning entry is 14 months back and does not count.
 - return_reason_share (parameter, cross-difficulty returns): return line reason not_as_pictured -> 75% (baseline 100% -> 30). Near-miss: the cancelled December return's line says changed_mind but refunded nothing.
 - service_recovery_share (parameter, cross-difficulty claims): refunded order carries the approved Damaged in Transit claim -> 80% (baseline -> 28).
 - unlimited_membership_share (parameter; plan and status sit on one Unlimited row, so it is not counted as multi-source): Unlimited Standard Annual, active -> 90% (baseline -> 25).
Goodwill (expected 378, all-baseline 400):
 - claim_type_grant_basis (method, cross-difficulty claims): Damaged in Transit -> twice the net points (108 after the reversal) = 216 < cap 400 (baseline start = per-case cap -> 400).
 - paid_delivery_uplift (parameter, multi-source plan in force AND fast service): Expedited 2-Day + active annual plan -> 40% (baseline -> 292).
 - repeat_failure_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty claims): compensation entries 2025-11-12 and 2026-07-15 -> exactly two -> 15% (baseline -> 346). Near-miss: the 2025-05-27 compensation is outside the 12 months.
 - membership_tenure_uplift (parameter): 98 whole months since 2018-05-03 -> 20% (baseline -> 335).
 Annual limit near-miss: the 400-point goodwill of 2025-11-14 is last calendar year and is NOT deducted (an agent using a trailing year would deduct it and still get 378 because 1200-400 > 378 — harmless); per-case cap 400 does not bind at 378 but binds without the reversal.

7. Base-invariant card. Reversal: membership_open (status active, membership row) and one_reversal_per_return_order (no loyalty_points_reversed row with this return_id/order_id). Goodwill: membership_active (active), documented_failure (claim CY status approved, order = linen-dress order), one_grant_per_claim (no service_goodwill row referencing CY; the only goodwill row references the November claim), once_per_reference (same), birthday_tenure time gate (anchor enrolled_date 2018-05-03, 30 calendar days inclusive; the 2026-07-31 posting is years past; just-before case 2018-06-01 fails, 2018-06-02 passes).

8. Business-object card. Target objects: claim CY (approved), its order (linen dress + trousers, Expedited 2-Day, 86.60 merchandise, card only), return RET (settled, line 2 trousers, 41.00 credited, grade A, no fee). Included: the order's earning entry (130 at 1.50) and the new reversal entry in the order's net points. Excluded: the replacement no-charge order (0.00, never earns), the cancelled return RC (no settlement), the November and May claims (other orders; only counted as compensation entries in the window), the 2025 goodwill row (other claim, other year).

9. Seed rationale. Customer + Gold membership whose whole tier history is on the ledger: welcome 500 at enrollment 2018-05-03, forfeited for inactivity on 2019-05-04 (no earning in the first 12 months); 2024 spend reached Silver on the 2024-09-20 posting (365.30); 2025 spend reached Gold on the 2025-06-18 posting (763.60; valid through 2026-12-31); the 2025-11-14 goodwill took available points to 2,011 and the nightly run converted 2,000 into a 20.00 Rewards Note (seeded as the credit instrument, expired unspent 2026-01-28). Balance 1018 = ledger sum; available points at frozen time 888. Eight earning entries tie to eight orders with card captures; the claim history (May missing item, November late delivery with a 24.95 shipping refund, July damaged dress with reship to a no-charge order) feeds the claim factors; the Unlimited Standard Annual plan feeds two factors. Automatic clauses checked: no conversion due (available 888 < 2,000), no inactivity forfeiture (last earning 2026-07-09), no tier change due (2026 spend 420.70 < Platinum; Gold valid through 2026-12-31), no missing earning (every dispatched order with spend has its earning entry), birthday in November (not due). PA does not tax clothing, so every order carries 0.00 tax.

10. Problem-tree card. Root loyalty_ext_delivery_failure_goodwill <- loyalty_ext_returned_merchandise_reversal; kind value_input; gate order_net_points; form state; sentence "The goodwill grant is fixed only after the points ledger carries a reversal entry for every refunded return made against the order the claim concerns." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; record-visible state (reversal entries on the ledger); no tool/id/code token; scope = every refunded return on that one order. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a loyalty_points_reversed entry: the reversal policy. Derivation: sentence + ledger (no reversal for RET) + reversal rule ("the agent posts the reversal for that return and order") -> post the reversal. Unmet at opening: return_cases.RET.status settled, refund -41.00 on 2026-07-21, order still at 130 points. Topological order: reversal, then acceptance. Deletion sensitivity (replay): skip the reversal -> grant 400 instead of 378. Persona never names the reversal or the trousers before the agent does. Tools validate nothing (no refusal path). The user write (acceptance) is the root and is handed over last.

11. Persona design. Tired, practical ER nurse; volunteers only the surface goal; credentials only when asked (email + mobile, DOB/ZIP as spare); one passive reaction to the reversal explanation (remembers the navy trousers), consent when asked, accepts the goodwill when handed the step, ends on the confirmation (the last gold action). She asks for nothing beyond the points for the damaged dress.

12. Standard solution. Locate (name) -> verify (email + mobile) -> membership -> claims -> claim events -> orders -> ledger -> returns -> settlements -> return lines -> order lines -> payments -> credit instruments and entries -> Unlimited plan -> reversal 22 -> hand over acceptance of 378.

13. Verification: gates run per task (check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff, check_cross_fire); check_compute recomputes 22 and 378 at handling time and every baseline figure listed above.

14. Draft recomputation from visible context only: the KB rules for the two policies + the reads listed give the same object (the approved claim, the settled return), the same order (reversal before grant) and the same figures; no second reading of the windows (12 months ending today, current calendar year) changes them in this world.


15. Revision log (round 2, policy-task audit). G1 symptom: goodwill only selects an approved claim while base allows approved or resolved -> root cause: undeclared narrowing -> change: rule sentence 'A goodwill grant is made while the claim stands approved, as part of making the member whole on it; a claim already resolved has had its compensation booked and is closed to a further goodwill grant.' plus an overwrite entry naming the base sentence -> re-run: all gates green, goodwill unchanged on this world (claim approved). T0-F1 symptom: seed claimed Gold reached on 2025-06-18 with 2025 spend 450.90 and an unforfeited 2018 welcome bonus -> root cause: tier and points history missing from the ledger -> change: seeded the 2019 inactivity forfeiture, the 2024 Silver-qualifying and 2025 Gold-qualifying orders with their earnings, lines and captures, moved the conversion to the night the 2025-11-14 goodwill crossed 2,000 available points (note expired unspent) and rewrote seed_consistency row by row -> re-run: REPLAY/SOLVABILITY/COMPUTE OK, scored values unchanged (the 12-month windows and the 2026 goodwill year do not reach the new rows). O1: the rules now state the floors the compute applies (restocking-fee deduction never below zero, return share zero without qualifying spend, net order points never below zero). O4: the edge condition now keys on refunded (settled) returns, as the sentence does. T0-O2: the Unlimited share is no longer described as multi-source.
user_scenario: You are Lucia Brennan, thirty-eight, an emergency-room nurse in Pittsburgh who does most of her Marlowe & Finch shopping on her phone between twelve-hour shifts; you are warm but a little tired, you speak in short practical sentences and you do not like being bounced around. Earlier this month the ivory linen wrap dress you ordered came with a torn seam. You reported it with photos, the damaged-item claim was approved and a replacement dress was sent to you. When you sorted the claim out you came away with the impression that Marlowe Rewards members sometimes get bonus points when a delivery goes wrong, and you have not seen anything like that on your account, so you are calling to ask for whatever Marlowe Rewards points you are due for that damaged dress and you would like it settled on this call. You open with exactly that, in your own words, and you do not offer anything else up front. You only give your details when the agent asks for them: your name is Lucia Brennan, your sign-in email is lucia.brennan@gmail.com and your mobile is 4125550112; if one more detail is needed your date of birth is 1987-11-09 and your billing ZIP is 15217. You do not know your claim number, order number or membership number by heart and say the agent will have to look them up. If the agent asks which order, you say it was the order with the linen dress, placed in early July. You do not know how many points you have or how the bonus is worked out, and you never suggest a number. If the agent tells you that points from something you sent back have to be taken off your account first, you remember the navy trousers from that same order that you returned because they looked nothing like the photos, and you say that is fine, go ahead. If the agent asks whether they may make changes on your rewards account to sort this out, you say yes. When the agent tells you the goodwill amount and hands you the step to accept it yourself, you accept it straight away for this damaged-dress claim, using exactly the details the agent reads out to you, and you do not haggle. Once you see the confirmation that the goodwill points are on your account, you thank the agent and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: Birthday, review, referral and goodwill bonuses post only while the membership is in status active (`suspension_withholds_rewards`); the welcome bonus posts with the enrollment itself.
A birthday bonus posts only if the membership is enrolled at least `birthday_bonus_min_tenure_days` calendar days before the bonus posting date.
Each bonus type posts at most once per bonus reference for a customer.

A goodwill grant requires a delivery claim on record for the referenced order whose status is approved or resolved; a late, lost or damaged parcel the customer only describes, without such a claim, is not a documented failure.
The bonus_reference is the claim's claim_id, and only one goodwill grant is posted per claim.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A birthday bonus posts only if the membership is enrolled at least `birthday_bonus_min_tenure_days` calendar days before the bonus posting date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Tenure days are counted as calendar days between the enrollment date and the posting date, and exactly the minimum qualifies.

boundary_check.just_before: Enrolled 2018-05-03; a posting date 29 calendar days after enrollment (2018-06-01) would fall short of the 30-day minimum and the bonus could not post.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A posting on 2018-06-02, exactly 30 calendar days after enrollment, qualifies (inclusive); the 2026-07-31 posting is about eight years later and qualifies.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's profile by the name she gives; returns her customer reference, contact details and date of birth.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and both writes are keyed on the customer reference; identity must be confirmed against this profile.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller owns the profile with two stated credentials (email and mobile).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account detail may be discussed and nothing written before identity is confirmed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the membership: tier Marlowe Rewards Gold, status active, enrollment date 2018-05-03.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes the per-case and annual goodwill caps; status active is the bonus gate; the enrollment date drives the membership-tenure uplift (goodwill) — and the reversal's earning-count tier uses the same ledger.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the member's delivery claims; select the one in status approved (Damaged in Transit Claim on the linen-dress order) and see the two older resolved claims.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The approved claim is the documented failure and the bonus reference; its type selects the grant-basis method; its order is the affected order; the reversal's service-recovery share reads the claim on the refunded order.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every evidence and compensation entry on the member's claims with their dates.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of compensation entries within the 12 months ending today sets the repeat-failure uplift (goodwill) and the service-recovery share (reversal); the May 2025 entry falls outside the window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's orders: the affected order shipped Expedited 2-Day, its merchandise subtotal and discount, and the replacement no-charge order.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The affected order's delivery service decides the paid-delivery uplift; its merchandise subtotal after discount is the denominator of the Rewards-Note share in the reversed spend.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every points entry: the affected order's earning entry (130 points at 1.50), earnings in the last 12 months, the 2025 goodwill entry and the absence of any reversal for the refunded return.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the prerequisite is unmet (no reversal entry for the settled return on the claim's order — the goodwill grant is fixed only after the points ledger carries a reversal entry for every refunded return made against the order the claim concerns); gives the original multiplier, the 12-month return share and earning count, the order's net points and the goodwill already posted this calendar year.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the member's returns: one settled Standard Return on the linen-dress order and one cancelled return from December 2025.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identifies the refunded return the reversal is owed for (the settled one) and excludes the cancelled return, which refunded nothing.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the settled return's credited merchandise (41.00), fee rows (none) and the card refund.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Fixes the reversed spend: merchandise credited less restocking fee withheld.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's returned lines: on the settled return the trousers line with reason not_as_pictured and grade A; the cancelled return's line never shipped back.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The line's reason sets the reason share of the reversal.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the booked lines of the member's orders: on the linen-dress order line 1 is the dress (damaged, reshipped at no charge) and line 2 the trousers (returned).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Ties the claim to the dress line and the return to the trousers line of the same order, so the refunded return is one made against the order the claim concerns.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the tenders captured and refunded on the member's orders; the linen-dress order was paid by card only.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows no Rewards Note amount captured on the affected order, so no note-paid share leaves the reversed spend.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's stored-value instruments: the 20.00 Rewards Note from the 2025-11-14 conversion, expired unspent on 2026-01-28.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms no Rewards Note value went to the linen-dress order (note-paid share zero).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the instrument entries: the note's load and its expiry forfeiture, no redemption.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms the note was never redeemed on any order, so no order of the member was part-paid with a note.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's Unlimited plan: Unlimited Standard Annual, status active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: An annual plan in force sets the membership share of the reversal and, with the Expedited service, the paid-delivery uplift of the goodwill.
First half of the unlock/call pair for the reversal write; no DB effect.

edges.condition: For every refunded return made against the approved claim's order (a return in status settled whose refund was issued), loyalty_ledger holds a loyalty_points_reversed row carrying that return_id and order_id.
edges.policy_source: The goodwill grant is fixed only after the points ledger carries a reversal entry for every refunded return made against the order the claim concerns.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The return on the claim's order is settled with a 41.00 merchandise refund paid on 2026-07-21, but the ledger holds no reversal entry for it; the order still shows its full 130 earned points.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The reversal call writes a loyalty_points_reversed row with return_id and order_id of the settled return; order_net_points falls from 130 to 108.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the reversal must land before the grant because the grant reads the order's net points; the reverse order credits 400 instead of 378 (verified by replay), so only reversal-then-grant matches gold.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reversal leaves order_net_points at 130: starting figure 260, x1.75 = 455, limited to the per-case cap 400 -> goodwill_points 400 instead of 378, and no reversal row in the terminal ledger (balance differs by 22 + 22).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for the points due for the damaged dress; it never mentions a reversal, the returned trousers, points being taken back or anything to settle first. The trousers come up only as a passive reaction after the agent says points from a returned item must be taken off first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: accept_goodwill_points_7ea0a08d creates the bonus row and updates the balance with whatever it is given; it never reads returns or reversals and has no refusal path, so it would credit a grant even with the reversal missing (the hash then differs).
